items.h: Geno Smith Is a Superflex Fallback Against Miami
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns in his first meeting with the Miami Dolphins. New York trailed throughout the second half in Week 7 and leaned more on Smith than it needed to in last week's win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Smith threw three touchdowns again in that game, finishing with 176 yards on just 21 attempts. Miami's run defense gives the Jets a reason to lean on Breece Hall and Braelon Allen again Sunday, and the Dolphins have allowed just two touchdown passes over their last three games. That makes it harder to count on Smith repeating last week's scoring output on so few throws. RotoBaller ranks Smith QB25 in its weekend update. The…

items.h: Geno Smith Surging After Big Win on the Road
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith broke out of a two-game lull with a huge performance against the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday. Smith only threw for 176 yards, but he added three passing touchdowns while playing turnover-free football. The veteran passer has now racked up three passing touchdowns in three different games this season, and two of them came in games against one-win opponents (Chargers and Dolphins). Fortunately for Smith, he's heading into another matchup against the Dolphins in Week 12, which gives him another opportunity to rank as a potential top-five quarterback in fantasy football. On the year, Smith is the QB15 in fantasy scoring, and that includes an ugly…

items.h: Geno Smith tosses three TDs in Week 11 win
items.s: Geno Smith completed 17 of his 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns while adding a four-yard run in a 27-24 win over the Chargers in Week 11. Smith was efficient in a game where the Jets leaned on the rushing attack to defeat the Chargers. Better yet, he showed no lingering effects of the ankle injury he suffered in Week 10. Two of his TDs went to Sterling Shepard, while the third went to Breece Hall. Sitting on 15 touchdowns and three interceptions this season, Smith will be a QB2 in fantasy in Week 12 vs. the Dolphins.

items.h: Tosses three TDs in Week 11 win
items.s: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards. Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice-squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the…

items.h: Geno Smith Set to Start With Superflex Appeal in Week 11
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) practiced in full Friday after being limited Thursday and listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated report. He carries no injury designation and will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards before leaving last week's loss to Buffalo. He threw for 165 yards at Kansas City the week before, and the Jets went without a touchdown in both games. RotoBaller ranks him QB20 for Week 11, putting him in play as a second quarterback in Superflex. Los Angeles gave up 340 passing yards to Jacoby Brissett on Monday, though he needed 49 attempts and threw no touchdowns. According to the Jets, Smith has…

items.h: Cleared to play Week 11
items.s: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

items.h: Cleared to play in Week 11

items.h: Geno Smith has No Designation, Will Play Sunday
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) has no injury designation for the Week 11 contest and will play on Sunday on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic. Smith suffered an ankle injury and was tested for a concussion in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills, but the 36-year-old veteran avoided any serious injuries and is in the clear to play this weekend as the Jets look to end their lengthy losing streak. While Smith has looked much better than he did in his disastrous 2025 campaign with the Las Vegas Raiders, he still profiles as a low-end QB2 in superflex fantasy leagues, and he will be without rookie…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) practicing in full Friday
items.s: Geno Smith (ankle) will practice in full on Friday. Smith was a limited participant at Thursday's practice session and will get in even more activity Friday. This suggests the veteran QB should be good to go for Sunday's matchup with the Chargers.

items.h: Looking good for Week 11
items.s: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.h: Geno Smith to Practice in Full Friday, Trending Towards Playing Sunday
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will practice in full on Friday and is trending toward being available for his team's Week 11 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, per ESPN's Rich Cimini. Smith suffered an ankle injury during New York's Week 10 loss to the Buffalo Bills that forced him to exit the game early, but it appears the veteran quarterback has avoided a serious issue. Across 10 games in 2026, Smith has completed 67.1% of his pass attempts for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns, and three interceptions. The Jets have a potentially higher-upside option behind Smith in fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik, who completed 11 of 20 pass attempts for 137 yards and an interception in…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) limited in practice Thursday
items.s: Geno Smith was limited in practice on Thursday. Smith has logged back-to-back limited practices. He is trending towards being good to go for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.h: Remains limited Thursday
items.s: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Smith also was deemed limited on Wednesday's practice estimate, so he may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Chargers without an injury designation. For his part, the Jets' QB1 isn't worried about his Week 11 availability, with Rich Cimini of ESPN.com noting Wednesday that while Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp at that point, the signal-caller stated that he intends to play this weekend. "That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

items.h: Geno Smith Limited Again on Thursday
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice for the second straight day on Thursday due to an ankle injury that knocked him out of Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills. Smith was also evaluated for a concussion in the same game, but tests on Monday ruled out any significant injuries for the 36-year-old veteran signal-caller. Smith said the plan is for him to start on Sunday on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, although he might be a little limited mobility-wise if his ankle is not 100%. After a two-week stretch against the division-rival Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders in which he threw five touchdown…

items.h: Limited, but plans to play Sunday
items.s: Smith (ankle), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, said afterward that he intends to play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Beyond noting that Smith will start if healthy, head coach Aaron Glenn hasn't confirmed that Smith will be available this weekend, but the quarterback's ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday is at least an encouraging sign for his status. Cimini notes that Smith was walking with a noticeable limp three days after injuring his left ankle in a Week 10 loss to the Bills, so the veteran signal-caller's mobility could be compromised to some degree if he gets the green light to play against the…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) limited on Wednesday
items.s: Geno Smith (ankle) gets in limited action at Wednesday's practice. Smith is dealing with an ankle injury that took him out of this past Sunday's game early. The issue is not severe, however, and the veteran QB was at least able to get in some activity Wednesday. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to start if Smith ultimately cannot go in Week 11.

items.h: Opening Week 11 with limited practice
items.s: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith (ankle) will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. Smith was unable to return to this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after tweaking his left ankle in the third quarter, but medical tests conducted after the game revealed no major injury. The veteran signal-caller will still be operating with a cap on his reps to begin Week 11 prep, and Glenn acknowledged that the Jets will wait and see how Smith fares as the week rolls along before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to start in Los Angeles if Smith isn't…

items.h: Teammate Says Geno Smith is "Good to Go"
items.s: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson believes that veteran quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will play this weekend in Los Angeles against the Chargers, according to Rich Cimini of ESPN. "From what I know, Geno feels good to go. You would have to ask him. From what I know, he's good to go. So I'll say that," Wilson said on Smith's status. Smith was checked for a concussion in Sunday's loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills before eventually being knocked out of the contest with an ankle injury. The 36-year-old is set for a limited practice on Wednesday, though, and all signs are pointing to him starting in Week 11 against the Chargers after tests earlier this week ruled out any…

items.h: Geno Smith to be Limited in Wednesday's Practice
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, head coach Aaron Glenn told Rich Cimini of ESPN. Smith was beat up in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills, getting knocked out of the game with an ankle injury while also being checked for a concussion after taking a hard hit. Tests on Monday cleared the 36-year-old veteran of any significant injuries, which means he is on the right side of questionable as the Jets prepare for the Los Angeles Chargers on the road this Sunday in Week 11. Smith was not a full practice participant to begin the week, but as long as he does not have any setbacks with his ankle this week, he should start…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) avoids major injury
items.s: Geno Smith underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal anything major. Smith will continue to be evaluated through the week. He will have a chance to be ready to go for Week 11.

items.h: Undergoes tests on ankle
items.s: Smith (ankle) underwent tests Monday that did not reveal any major injuries, but he will continue to be evaluated during the week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Smith was checked for a concussion in Sunday's loss to the Bills but was cleared and returned to the game before then suffering an ankle injury. He finished the game 13 of 21 passing for 148 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. It sounds like Smith has a good chance to suit up next Sunday against the Chargers, but if he's not cleared, then rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to make the start.

items.h: Geno Smith's Tests Reveal No Major Injuries
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle), who dealt with ankle and head injuries in the team's Week 10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal anything major, sources told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Smith, whose ankle is the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week, but so far, everything looks good. The 36-year-old took a hard hit against Buffalo and was evaluated for a concussion on Sunday before eventually returning, only to injure his ankle and be ruled out for the rest of the contest. He finished the day 13-for-21 passing for just 148 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. Head coach Aaron Glenn told the…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) to undergo MRI Monday
items.s: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith will undergo an MRI on Monday. Smith left Sunday's game early against the Bills with an ankle injury. There should be an update on his status later this week.

items.h: Set for MRI on ankle
items.s: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith will get further imaging on his left ankle Monday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports. Glenn said that he won't have an update on Smith's status until later in the week once his MRI results are read, but the coach noted that Smith -- if healthy -- will remain the Jets' starting quarterback heading into next Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith played less than half of the Jets' offensive snaps in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, missing time while getting checked for a concussion and then due to the ankle injury. Backup Cade Klubnik finished out the game under center in place of Smith, who completed 13 of 21…

items.h: Geno Smith Will Remain Jets Starter if Healthy
items.s: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will remain the team's starting quarterback if he's healthy. Smith suffered an ankle injury in the 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and didn't return, prompting rookie Cade Klubnik to enter the lineup. Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards and one interception, and added three carries for 26 yards on the ground. With Smith set to remain the Jets' starting quarterback, his health is a major question, as he's scheduled to undergo an MRI on his ankle. Glenn wouldn't speculate on his game status for Week 11's matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, but if he misses time, Klubnik would start in his place.…

items.h: Status for Week 11 uncertain
items.s: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after Sunday's loss to Buffalo that Smith, who departed the contest due to an ankle injury, will have his status for Week 11 determined during the upcoming week of practice, Jack Bell of the Jets' official site reports. Smith was hurt during New York's final offensive series of the first half Sunday when he was hit by a pair of defenders while throwing an incomplete pass. He was placed in concussion protocol and passed, clearing the way for him to return to the game. However, Smith then exited again after hurting his ankle, and this time he was unable to return. The veteran quarterback's practice activity, if any, during Week 11 prep will likely determine…

items.h: Geno Smith (ankle) exits Sunday's game early
items.s: Geno Smith (ankle) exited Sunday's gam early and did not return. He completed 13-of-21 passes for 148 yards prior to his injury. Smith also exited the game to be evaluated for a concussion, but returned briefly before suffering an ankle injury. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status ahead of a Week 11 game with the Chargers.

items.h: Won't finish Sunday's game
items.s: Smith (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. After previously exiting the contest and then clearing the NFL's concussion protocol, Smith is now done for the day with an ankle issue after completing 13 of 21 pass attempts for 148 yards. Once again, Cade Klubnik has been summoned to fill in for Smith, whose status will need to be closely monitored as next Sunday's game against the Chargers approaches.

items.h: Hurts ankle Sunday
items.s: Smith headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Bills after injuring his ankle, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Smith, who previously exited the game to be checked for a head injury and subsequently cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and returned to the field, but now an ankle issue has him deemed questionable to resume action by the Jets. As a result, Cade Klubnik is back in at QB for New York.

items.h: Back in Sunday's game
items.s: Smith has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and has returned to Sunday's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports. Smith previously exited the contest and headed to the blue medical tent after absorbing a hard hit, but after being checked out he's back in there at QB for the Jets. While Smith was sidelined, Cade Klubnik subbed in for him, completing two of four passes for 39 yards and rushing twice for 19 yards.

Geno Smith being evaluated for a concussion
items.s: Jets QB Geno Smith is currently being evaluated for a concussion. Smith was hit hard ending the second quarter. Cade Klubnik is currently in at quarterback for the Jets.

items.h: Heads to medical tent Sunday
items.s: Smith exited Sunday's game against the Bills and headed to the blue medical tent after absorbing a hard hit, Connor Hughes of SNY reports. Prior to that, Smith completed nine of 16 passes for 113 yards. It remains to be seen if the QB is back out there for second half of the contest, but on the plus side, Hughes notes that Smith subsequently returned to the team's bench as opposed to going to the locker room.

items.h: Geno Smith Ruled Out With Ankle Injury
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's home game against the Buffalo Bills. Smith, 36, did not start the second half after taking a hard hit at the end of the second quarter. He briefly returned in the third after clearing concussion protocol, but limped back to the medical tent after one drive. The veteran completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards and no touchdowns before exiting Sunday's game. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik, who had only played in the season opener, took over for Smith to start the second half and remains in the game.

items.h: Geno Smith Questionable to Return with Ankle Injury
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with an apparent ankle injury. The 36-year-old veteran previously exited the Week 10 matchup after taking a hard hit at the end of the first half. He briefly returned in the third quarter after clearing concussion protocol, but was seen limping back to the medical tent after one drive and subsequently went to the locker room. Smith completed 13 of 21 pass attempts for 148 yards before exiting the game. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik started the second half for Smith and is playing in just his second game of the season.

items.h: Geno Smith Back in Medical Tent vs. Bills
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (undisclosed) went back to the medical tent in the third quarter of his team's Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. The 36-year-old veteran previously went to the tent after a hit late in the first half of Sunday's home game, and he briefly returned in the third quarter after clearing concussion protocol. Smith completed 11 of 18 passes for 145 yards before going into the tent a second time. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik started the second half, completing two of four passes for 39 yards before Smith briefly returned.

items.h: Geno Smith Goes to Medical Tent After Late First-Half Hit
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith went to the medical tent after taking a hit on a third-down incompletion with 25 seconds left in the first half of Sunday's Week 10 game against the Buffalo Bills. Trainers helped Smith off the field, and he returned to the bench before halftime, according to Zack Rosenblatt. Smith completed nine of 16 passes for 113 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. He took one sack before leaving. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik replaced Smith, who is being evaluated for a concussion.

items.h: No TDs in Week 9 loss
items.s: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards. Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

items.h: Geno Smith held in check in Week 9 loss
items.s: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 pass attempts for 165 yards in a 35-12 loss to the Jets. He added eight rushing yards on one carry. Smith and the Jets' offense failed to get anything consistent going, stalling out and having to settle for field goals in their scoring chances. This did break a streak of seven straight games with at least one passing touchdown for the veteran. Smith and the Jets will take on the Bills in Week 10.

items.h: Geno Smith Loses Top Target Ahead of Week 9
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will face the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday without Garrett Wilson (concussion), who leads the team with 43 catches and 527 receiving yards. Smith threw for 290 yards and two touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 8, averaging 9.1 yards per attempt. The Jets have scored 25 and 33 points over their last two games, and Smith has thrown 12 touchdown passes against three interceptions this season. His 15 completions on passes traveling at least 20 yards in the air are tied for the league lead. Adonai Mitchell, coming off a 142-yard game, gives Smith another receiver who can win downfield. Kansas City has allowed seven passing touchdowns in seven games, though…

Smith threw second-quarter touchdown passes of 18 yards to Isaiah Williams and 12 yards to Adonai Mitchell while coming 10 yards shy of his second 300-yard passing performance of the season. The veteran QB had a chance to orchestrate a game-winning drive against his former team, but the Jets' comeback bid came up short when Smith threw an end-zone interception from the Raiders' 35-yard line with seven seconds remaining. Smith has been picked off in each of his last three outings after going without an interception through five starts…

Smith and the Jets will take on the Raiders in Week 8.

items.h: Three TDs not enough in Week 7
items.s: Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins. He also rushed twice for no gain and threw a successful two-point conversion. Smith matched Miami's opening-drive touchdown with a 13-yard touchdown pass to Mason Taylor on the Jets' first drive, but the veteran QB threw an interception deep in Dolphins territory on the next drive. The Jets trailed for the entirety of the last three quarters, allowing Smith to rack up some big numbers during their failed comeback bid, as he posted his second three-touchdown performance of the season. He found Omar Cooper for a three-yard touchdown in the third quarter after they…

He completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards, a touchdown, and an interception against the New England Patriots in Week 6, bringing his season totals to 1,336 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and one interception with a 68.9% completion rate. Adonai Mitchell's return gives him another receiving option alongside Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. He has thrown multiple touchdown passes only once this season and has…

items.h: Geno Smith has Put Himself on the QB2 Streaming Radar
items.s: New York Jets veteran quarterback Geno Smith is playing much better than he did last year with the Las Vegas Raiders. In his first six games with the Jets, the two-time Pro Bowler has completed 68.9% of his 177 pass attempts for 1,336 yards, seven touchdowns, and only one interception. The lack of interceptions is particularly noteworthy after Smith tossed a league-high 17 picks in 15 starts for the Raiders in his lone year in Sin City. The 36-year-old went 20-for-30 for 252 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday's 26-19 Week 6 loss to the division-rival New England Patriots. Smith did not have eye-popping numbers, but he was impressive nevertheless and brought the Jets back…

items.h: Solid numbers despite loss
items.s: Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding two rushes for minus-1 yard in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday. Smith took three sacks while trying to play catch-up all afternoon, and in that context, his final numbers were all the more impressive. The veteran signal-caller helped the Jets claw back from a 17-3 halftime deficit to get within four entering the fourth quarter, but his interception at the Patriots' 24-yard line early in the period snuffed out a potential scoring opportunity. Smith has certainly given New York some much-needed veteran stability at the quarterback position and displayed encouraging chemistry with…

items.h: Geno Smith tosses one touchdown in Week 6 loss
items.s: Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 pass attempts for 252 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in a 26-19 loss to the Patriots. Smith connected with Omar Cooper Jr. on a deep pass for the Jets' lone passing touchdown of the day. Smith spread the ball around effectively and was intercepted for the first time this season. The Jets and Smith will take on Miami at home in Week 7.

items.h: Geno Smith Difficult to Trust Against New England
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith has completed 69.4% of his passes for 1,084 yards, six touchdowns, and no interceptions through five games, but those numbers have not translated into consistently useful fantasy performances. He managed only 182 passing yards and one touchdown against Cleveland in Week 5, marking his second consecutive outing below 200 yards. Protection remains another concern, with Smith already taking 16 sacks this season. The Jets now travel to New England to face a Patriots defense coming off an impressive performance against Las Vegas, which managed just 17 points in Week 5. Smith's connection with Garrett Wilson provides some upside, but New York has not…

items.h: Geno Smith Offers Limited Waiver Appeal Ahead of Week 6
items.s: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is worth rostering as depth in Superflex and two-quarterback leagues, but he is difficult to justify as a Week 6 pickup in standard one-QB formats. Smith completed 17 of 30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over Cleveland, marking his second consecutive outing below 200 passing yards. He has totaled just 301 yards and two touchdowns over those two games after throwing for 321 yards and three scores against Detroit in Week 3. Through five starts, the 36-year-old has completed 69.4% of his passes for 1,084 yards, six touchdowns, and no interceptions. However, he has also taken 16 sacks while contributing only 43 rushing yards,…

items.h: Modest numbers in rainy Week 5 win
items.s: Smith completed 17 of 30 pass attempts for 182 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns. He also rushed five times for seven yards and lost a fumble. Smith threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to Garrett Wilson on the team's first drive, but New York's passing game was quiet the rest of the way while playing through rainy conditions for the second time in as many home games. The veteran QB, who celebrated his 36th birthday Saturday, has a tidy 6:0 TD:INT, though Smith has put the ball on the ground in all but one game while losing two of four fumbles. Smith and the Jets will hope to get some of their injured skill-position players back in Week 6 against the Patriots. Kenyon…

items.h: Smith completed eight of 15 pass attempts for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
items.s: Smith threw for just 18 yards in the first half as the Jets took a 13-3 deficit into the locker room. Things didn't get much better offensively after halftime, except for Smith's 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith has a 5:0 TD:INT and is averaging 226 passing yards heading into a Week 5 home game against the Browns.

items.h: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
items.s: The veteran QB was almost flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

items.h: Smith completed 27 of 41 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers. He also rushed five times for 17 yards.
items.s: Smith navigated the Jets to a 17-7 lead with 11:04 remaining in the fourth quarter, but New York's offense stalled down the stretch, with a turnover on downs sandwiched around two punts on the team's final three possessions. Making his first home start for the Jets in nearly a decade, Smith threw his first touchdown pass of the season on a five-yard connection with Garrett Wilson in the third quarter. Smith hasn't turned the ball over but has just 462 passing yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Lions, who allowed three touchdown passes apiece to Tyler Shough and Josh Allen.

items.h: Smith completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards while rushing six times for seven yards in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans.
items.s: Smith kept the offense on schedule but wasn't asked to do too much as the Jets rode their running game and defense to a convincing Week 1 win. There will likely be more pass-heavy game scripts to come, possibly as soon as Week 2 against the Packers, but Smith gave the Jets refreshingly competent quarterback play despite his modest yardage total to win the first game of his second stint with the team. Smith showed a nice connection with wide receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, connecting with them on nine of 10 targets for 139 yards.

items.h: Smith was voted a Jets captain by his teammates ahead of the 2026 season, Amanda Vogt and Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
items.s: It's been nearly 10 years since Smith last took a snap for the Jets, but after revitalizing his career with the Seahawks and Raiders over the last four seasons, he's back in New York as a grizzled vet with age (34) and experience on his side. Smith recorded at least 3,000 yards and 19 touchdowns through the air in each of those four campaigns, but he also tossed 52 interceptions in 64 regular-season games during that span. Picks are often an issue for Smith, but he at least will have a nice skill-position group of RB Breece Hall (groin), WRs Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper…

items.h: Smith will not play in Friday's preseason finale against the Giants, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.s: Smith and most of the Jets' starters will sit out Friday's contest as the team prepares for Week 1 against the Titans on Sunday, Sept. 13. The quarterback played the opening drive of the team's preseason win over Pittsburgh on Aug. 21, completing all seven of his passes for 65 yards and a touchdown. That will end up being the only action he sees during the preseason, and Week 1 will be his first regular-season start with the Jets since 2016.

items.h: Smith completed all seven of his pass attempts for 65 yards and a touchdown in Friday's 17-0 preseason win over the Steelers.
items.s: After sitting out the preseason opener due to a sore ankle, Smith saw the first game action of his second stint with the Jets. He played only the opening drive but was sharp during his brief time in the game, completing all seven of his passes to six different targets, including a 13-yard touchdown pass to Jelani Woods. Smith looks like he's in midseason form already, so it remains to be seen if the veteran QB will get any action in next Friday's preseason finale against the Giants.

items.h: Smith is scheduled to start Friday's preseason game against the Steelers, Connor Hughes of SNYtv reports.
items.s: Smith sat out the Jets' preseason opener due to a sore ankle, paving the way for rookie fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik to get the start. The veteran starter has since recovered and is set for the first game action of his second stint with the Jets. Smith sits safely atop the team's QB depth chart, while Klubnik looks like the favorite to secure the backup role over Bailey Zappe and Brady Cook.

items.h: Smith (ankle) was a full participant in Monday's training camp practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Smith was spotted wearing a sleeve on his lower leg and was limping slightly at times during Monday's practice. Still, it was a positive sign from the veteran quarterback, who did not play in the Jets' preseason opener against the Buccaneers this past Friday due to left ankle soreness. It remains to be seen whether Smith and the other starters will play in the Jets' next preseason game, which takes place this Friday on the road against the Steelers.

items.h: Smith (ankle) was on the field for Monday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Per Cimini, Smith -- who didn't play in this past Friday's preseason game against the Buccaneers -- sported a sleeve on his lower left leg as he participated in Monday's walkthrough. It remains to be seen if the QB will be limited at practice in the coming days, but either way, Smith's next chance to see game action arrives this Friday against the Steelers.

items.h: Coach Aaron Glenn said after Friday's 24-16 preseason loss to the Buccaneers that Smith sat out the contest due to a sore ankle and is day-to-day, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Per Glenn, Smith picked up the injury during the Jets' joint practice with Tampa Bay on Wednesday. Considering Smith is deemed day-to-day, the Jets likely will exercise caution with him until he's back to 100 percent. In any case, his next opportunity for exhibition action is next Friday at Pittsburgh.

items.h: Smith won't play in Friday's preseason game against the Buccaneers due to a sore foot, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.s: On Tuesday, coach Aaron Glenn told Al Iannazzone of Newsday that Smith and the rest of the Jets' starters would log some snaps Friday. While an injury to Smith has quelled those plans, the team isn't concerned about it, and he'd play through it if it was the regular season. Instead, New York will take a cautious approach with its starting quarterback, meaning his next chance for exhibition action is next Friday at Pittsburgh.

items.h: Coach Aaron Glenn noted Tuesday that the Jets' starters, a group that includes Smith, will play in Friday's preseason opener against the Buccaneers, Al Iannazzone of Newsday reports.
items.s: It remains to be seen how much work Smith will see Friday, but after the veteran QB gets his reps in, Cade Klubnik, Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe are candidates to see action against Tampa Bay. As the coming campaign approaches, Smith is slated to lead a New York offense paced by top RB Breece Hall and which features a diverse pass-catching group that includes WRs Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, as well as TEs Kenyon Sadiq (hernia) and Mason Taylor.

items.h: Smith is the clear top quarterback for the Jets, but a battle between Bailey Zappe, Cade Klubnik and Brady Cook is ongoing for the second spot on the depth chart, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Smith will likely dominate first-team reps leading up to the regular season, but the Jets will use training camp and preseason play to evaluate their backup options. Of the team's other quarterbacks, Klubnik probably has the best chance of seeing the field eventually in 2026, as the Jets could be motivated to evaluate their 2026 fourth-round pick in meaningful game situations if the team falls out of playoff contention again on the heels of a 3-14 season in 2025.
